items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read the hook payload before claiming a restored orchestrator seat**

For a persisted managed Herdr pair, `--attach` calls this `--self` path and immediately exits at line 1362, so it is the only opportunity to refresh the seat lock. The SessionStart command inherits Claude Code's JSON hook payload on stdin but this script never parses it, and neither `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` nor `CLAUDE_PID` is populated anywhere in the runtime configuration. Consequently this path emits `seat_claim=unresolved`; a restored session keeps a stale/bare lock and the Stop-hook check continues to drop worker delivery. Parse the hook payload and obtain the live pane PID (or use the same Herdr lookup as the non-self path) before claiming.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:50ebfdc

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read the SessionStart payload on macOS**

On macOS, where the default toolchain does not provide GNU `timeout`, this guard skips reading stdin entirely. For a SessionStart invocation whose session ID is only present in Claude's JSON payload and whose Herdr `agent list` entry is not yet populated, `sid` stays empty and the managed pane emits `seat_claim=unresolved` rather than replacing its bare lock, so Stop-hook delivery remains suppressed after a restore. Use a portable bounded read (or an available macOS equivalent) rather than making payload parsing conditional on `timeout`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:99d734b

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replace stale composite locks on session restore**

When a persisted Herdr session resumes in a new Claude process, the new SessionStart claim uses `<sid>.<new_pid>` but the previous `<sid>.<old_pid>` remains held. This condition releases only a bare `sid`, so the retry is skipped and the lock stays stale; the Stop hook then compares against the new composite owner and continues to suppress worker delivery. Fresh evidence: this revision now creates composite owners on every initial launch, making the next restore hit this unhandled composite-lock case. Accept a prior owner matching the same session ID and release that exact owner before retrying the claim.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:63d4e03

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate seat claims to the orchestrator pane**

The managed SessionStart hook invokes `herdr-agents --attach` for every Claude session in a Herdr pane, but this claim runs before the later worker-pane/worktree checks. Consequently, a Claude session in any other main-checkout pane can claim the unsuffixed orchestrator identity with its own `<sid>.<pid>`; if it wins the startup/restore race (for example with a legacy main-checkout Claude worker), the actual orchestrator subsequently gets `status=held` and its turn delivery remains suppressed. Verify that `HERDR_PANE_ID` is the orchestrator pane before claiming.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/e4903a1e03ff720ae31dd59b53c9f96df8479ef8/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:9b658a9

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent the dispatch allow rule from authorizing command chains**

The exclusion is explicitly matched only on the command's first word, while this wildcard allow rule approves the whole Bash invocation. A Claude worker can therefore issue `agmsg-dispatch ...; <arbitrary command>`: the first word exempts the invocation from the sandbox and the allow rule suppresses the permission prompt, letting the trailing command run outside the configured write and network limits. Use a fixed-purpose wrapper or otherwise reject shell operators instead of auto-allowing the command prefix.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L79](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/e4903a1e03ff720ae31dd59b53c9f96df8479ef8/AGENTS.md#L78-L79)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: not-applicable:refuted by the Claude Code permissions documentation ("Compound commands": Claude Code is aware of shell operators, so a rule like Bash(safe-cmd *) will not permit safe-cmd && other-cmd; a rule must match each subcommand independently), fetched and verified by the orchestrator 2026-10-01; excludedCommands matches the first word only, so a chained command leaves the sandbox but still prompts for the unmatched subcommand; the manifest comment quotes the docs (9b658a9)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the hook payload on macOS**

On macOS, when Claude leaves the SessionStart pipe open and Herdr has not yet exposed the pane's agent session, `read -t -d ''` waits for EOF/NUL and Bash 3.2 discards the partial JSON on timeout. `HOOK_SESSION_ID` is therefore empty, the unavailable `herdr agent list` fallback cannot supply it, and the hook emits `seat_claim=unresolved`, leaving restored turn delivery suppressed. Fresh evidence: the new test itself documents Bash 3.2's discard behavior but only passes because its fake Herdr lookup already returns the same session ID.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:9b658a9

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate stale lock PIDs before preserving them**

On a persisted-session restore, if the former Claude PID has exited and the OS has recycled that PID for an unrelated process, `ps -p` succeeds and this branch leaves the old `<sid>.<old-pid>` lock in place. The new Claude instance then reports `seat_claim=failed`, while the Stop hook compares against `<sid>.<new-pid>` and continues suppressing delivery. Fresh evidence: the new stale-lock recovery uses only process existence here, without verifying that the PID is the live Claude instance for this pane/session.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body:
The following taps are not trusted:
  aws/tap
  azure/bicep
  hashicorp/tap

Homebrew is currently ignoring formulae, casks and commands from these taps because tap trust is required.

Prefer trusting only the specific formulae, casks or commands you need.
Trust installed formulae from these taps with:
  brew trust --formula azure/bicep/bicep
  brew trust --formula hashicorp/tap/packer
Trust other specific casks and commands with:
  brew trust --cask <user>/<tap>/<cask>
  brew trust --command <user>/<tap>/<command>
Whole-tap trust is broader and includes all current and future formulae,
casks and commands from the listed taps. Trust whole taps with:
  brew trust aws/tap azure/bicep hashicorp/tap
Untap them with:
  brew untap aws/tap azure/bicep hashicorp/tap
To disable trust checks:
  export HOMEBREW_NO_REQUIRE_TAP_TRUST=1
This is not recommended and will be removed in a later release.
For more information, see:
  https://docs.brew.sh/Tap-Trust
